 “We’re just going to confront that and go for it” – Arteta ready for Bayern challenge
 Champions League Press conferences Manager Men 
 @AAllenSport 
 October 20, 2026 
 14 
 Mikel Arteta is looking forward to a different kind of test against Bayern Munich, with Arsenal heading to the Allianz Arena intent on taking the game to the German champions.
 The Gunners have faced growing scrutiny over their performances while grinding out results domestically in recent weeks, often against opponents content to defend deep. Bayern, who have scored 36 goals in 10 games this season, are unlikely to take that approach, and Arteta welcomes the challenge.
 “We’re really looking forward to the game; this is the stage, this is the kind of team, this is the kind of coach, this is the kind of club, the stadium that you want to be involved in.
 “We have prepared for the game with lots of enthusiasm, and I’m really thrilled to come here and win the game tomorrow.”
 Last season’s meeting at the Emirates – a 3-1 win for the Gunners – gave Arteta a taste of what to expect, and he anticipates another demanding encounter.
 “We know the kind of game that we are going to play; I think both teams are very clear on that, and we experienced that at the Emirates [last season], and it’s going to be a very similar one in many moments. Especially, we have the level of connection and positiveness in and around the team, so yeah, very excited about it.”
 It remains unclear whether Vincent Kompany will be in the Bayern dugout tomorrow. The head coach is suffering from a virus that has affected his legs , while there are also doubts over the fitness of veteran goalkeeper Manuel Neuer. Michael Olise will definitely miss out after being sent off in Bayern’s last Champions League game against Bodo/Glimt.
 Asked whether the Frenchman’s absence would help Arsenal, Arteta made clear he would rather face opponents at full strength. Even without Olise, he sees plenty to admire, and plenty to prepare for.
 “You want to face the best players in these kinds of games, and he’s out, but when you look at their squad and the starting possible XI that they have, you know, first of all, as a team, one, how incredibly well coached they are, the mindset that they have, the conviction that they have in every action, and then individual quality moments that they can create throughout the games when you look at the goals and chances that they generate.
 “So that’s the opposition that you want to be facing, and we will be facing tomorrow, and we’re just going to confront that and go for it.”
 Arteta knows Kompany well from their time together at Manchester City, and his admiration for the Belgian was accompanied by concern over his health.
 “I hope that he gets better soon. I hope that he’s there tomorrow, because it will be very good for the game that his presence is there.
 “Huge admirer of him, one as a person, because I got to know him, I worked with him for a few years, and then what he’s done as a coach, his career, where he started at first in Belgium, then at Burnley, and now what he’s doing here, because I think the identity and the quality that his team shows in the last few years, it’s another level, and that’s a big credit for him.”
 For all Bayern’s attacking quality, Arsenal arrive with a defensive partnership earning plenty of praise. After Sunday’s match at the City Ground, Nottingham Forest’s Oliver Glasner described Ezri Konsa and Gabriel Magalhaes as the best centre-back pairing in world football.
 The assessment went down well with Arteta, who joked: “That’s a great opinion. For me, my players are the best in the world, and I think the partnership that they have developed in such a short period of time is remarkable.
 “Credit to both of them, credit to the rest of the team as well, but I think on Sunday both of them, specifically in key moments they were exceptional again.”
 Their next task is to contain Harry Kane, whose form for club and country over the past 12 months has made him one of the favourites to win the Ballon d’Or next week. The ex-Gunner will provide another measure of just how good Arsenal’s partnership has become.
 “Well, they get tested a lot in the Premier League certainly, and they have already done [the same] in the Champions League,” said Arteta.
 “I think what Harry is doing and he’s done in the last few years, it’s just something else, another level and that’s the level they’re going to have to face tomorrow.”
 At this stage of the competition, victory would be welcome rather than essential. But there was little in Arteta’s demeanour or words to suggest he sees this as a game Arsenal can afford to let pass them by. With 14 consecutive league phase wins behind them, the Gunners head to Munich intent on claiming another Bayern scalp.
